text:
maria: Quick heads-up: ruby sampleapp calls to Redwood fail when using OIDC tokens. Upstream returns 400.
elaine: Any logs or raw requests?
maria: App log shows: 
```
Net::HTTPBadResponse (wrong status line: "GET /v1/...")
```
sam: That usually means the request was malformed. Can you dump the raw HTTP headers?
maria: I captured the request. The Authorization header ends partway through the JWT (token is ~3.2k chars). Looks truncated.
ryan: Where's the sampleapp running? Could be the ingress/proxy trimming long headers.
maria: Local docker-compose with a small envoy proxy in front. If I bypass the proxy and hit the backend directly the token is intact and calls succeed.
elaine: Envoy's defaults shouldn't clip that small token, but a stray newline or control char in the header value could cause the proxy to treat it as folded and drop the remainder.
sam: Good point. Grep the auth helper for any accidental newlines.
maria: Found it: `headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{token}\n"` in the auth connector. Removing the trailing newline fixes the request through the proxy.
ryan: Newline in header value -> folded header behavior in proxies. Classic gotcha.
elaine: Proposal: sanitize tokens before setting headers (e.g. `token.strip` or `token.gsub(/[\r\n]/, '')`) and add a unit that asserts header values contain no control chars.
sam: Also add a tiny quickstart troubleshooting note re: proxies and long JWTs. The Go sample already trims whitespace; keep parity.
ryan: I'll open a small PR against sampleapp: trim token, add unit test, update Quickstart blurb.
devops-bot: CI queued: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/5555 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
devops-bot: CI passed: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/5555 :white_check_mark:
maria: Will validate against our enterprise ingress tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
